challenges.name: dual-write-both-orders
challenges.title: The dual-write problem: where the gap is
challenges.description: Two versions of the CodeDev enroll handler, one per order of the two writes. Decide for each statement whether it holds for the code and the failure shown.

questions.explanation: True. The commit is durable, so the row survives the kill. The fact that an event still has to be sent lives only in the memory of the killed process: the loop, its attempt counter and the enrollment object disappear with it, and nothing after a restart knows about this enrollment. Retries only help with failures the process survives, and even then only for outages shorter than about 6 seconds here. The common misconception is that "retry with backoff" makes the publish reliable; it makes it more likely, not guaranteed. A durable record of the pending event (an outbox row in the same commit) is what survives the kill.

False. Only operations that go through tx take part in the PostgreSQL transaction. The broker acknowledged the message at .219, so it is in the broker's log, and a rollback in PostgreSQL has no way to remove it. Consumers will process an event for an enrollment that was rolled back: a ghost event. Publishing inside the callback is really the order publish-then-commit, and it adds two more problems: the transaction (with its locks and pooled connection) stays open during a network call, and a broker outage now blocks every enrollment. The misconception is that code placed inside a transaction callback is automatically transactional.
